memory: A study found that "Singing Training" significantly reduced Neuropsychiatric Inventory scores compared to a control group (p = 0.042). Methods included paired t-test, Wilcoxon, and nonparametric tests. Participants provided voice samples through standardized procedures, while the control group maintained daily routines. Exclusions were major depression and prior Sonas sessions.

memory: A double-blinded, randomized trial compared Ropivacaine-fentanyl-clonidine (RFC) with Ropivacaine-fentanyl (RF) on hemodynamic parameters. memory: A study compared bimatoprost 0.03% preservative-free (PF) with bimatoprost 0.03% (Lumigan) on intraocular pressure (IOP). memory: Study [PMC5781260] was a double-blind, randomized controlled trial assessing lemon verbena extract (Recoverben®) on muscle strength and recovery after exhaustive exercise. The extract from Aloysia citriodora significantly reduced the decline in maximal voluntary contraction (MVC) compared to placebo (p = 0.0311), with a significant time effect (p = 0.0051). The extract was free of banned substances and marketed as a sports nutrition product. Findings support the hypothesis that lemon verbena extract may aid in exercise-induced muscle damage and recovery.

memory: The SCOPE trial is an RCT in Ontario, Canada, comparing colorectal cancer screening interventions. Eligibility was confirmed via physician forms and nurse reviews. Participants were randomized to telephone or mail follow-up using de-identified lists. Biweekly venous blood samples were collected for hematological and biochemical assessments, and pregnancy tests were conducted for females of childbearing potential. A genome-wide analysis in European ancestry individuals identified significant SNPs on chromosome 11 associated with bisoprolol response. Endometrial biopsies were obtained via hysteroscopy and D&C, with participants randomized to LNG-IUS or NET and monitored using TVS and Pipelle sampling. Ethics approval and MHRA authorization were obtained for these trials.
text: The SCOPE trial found that bisoprolol showed a significant association with SNPs on chromosome 11 (rs2514036, rs948445, rs2514037) related to ASBP response, compared to losartan/amlodipine/hydrochlorothiazide. This suggests genetic variability may influence drug efficacy.
outcome: SNPs on chromosome 11 (rs2514036, rs948445, and rs2514037) provided evidence for association reaching genome‐wide significance for ASBP (systolic blood pressure) response

Patients avoided certain topical treatments during the study.

memory: A pilot RCT in southwest England compared a weight management intervention (diet, physical activity, plus usual care) with usual care (antidepressant/mood stabilizer treatment) on fiber intake at 12 months. The intervention, involving group meetings, skill-building, and self-regulatory strategies, significantly increased fiber intake by 5.7 g/day (p < .001), correlating with weight loss at 4 and 12 months. Randomization used sealed envelopes, with fidelity checks and qualitative data. Participants received feedback and action plans. The study aimed to test behavior change mechanisms and refine the model for future trials.

memory: Gepotidacin, a DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV inhibitor, was studied in phase II for ABSSSI and gonorrhea, showing minimal human enzyme impact. memory: A study compared LPA (30 min moderate-intensity, 5-7 days/week) with FME (education control) on pain in FM patients. Post-testing showed LPA significantly reduced pain (P = .006; Cohen's d = .67) compared to FME. Participants received LPA training, self-monitoring, and strategies to manage barriers. Pain and FIQ scores were measured, and LPA types were logged. The protocol addressed FM-specific challenges. Control group received education only. Exclusion criteria included medication changes, anxiety/depression treatment plans, and time commitment issues. The study was approved by Johns Hopkins IRB, with informed consent obtained.
text: LPA significantly reduced pain (P = .006; Cohen's d = .67) compared to FME in FM patients. The LPA group engaged in 30 minutes of moderate-intensity activity 5-7 days/week, while the FME group received only education. This suggests LPA is more effective than education alone in managing FM-related pain.

memory: Green tea (GT) was tested against placebo in double-blind crossover trials on trained and untrained males to assess its effect on post-exercise fat oxidation. One study reported significantly higher fat oxidation in the GT group (p < 0.01). Participants consumed GT or placebo before exercise, with a washout period of at least two weeks. Measurements included blood lactate, lipid levels, and heart rate. The study involved aerobically trained cyclists, triathletes, and untrained males. The design included randomization, blinding, ethical approval, and informed consent. Results suggest GT may enhance post-exercise fat oxidation, but more research on diverse populations is needed.
text: Green tea may enhance post-exercise fat oxidation compared to placebo, as shown in a double-blind crossover trial (p < 0.01). The study included trained and untrained males, with measurements of blood lactate, lipid levels, and heart rate. However, more research on diverse populations is needed to confirm these findings.

memory: A phase III, open, multicenter study evaluated Lan ATG injections (3-5 doses) in patients as their own controls. memory: A study compared "Pro Taper universal retreatment" and "Mani NRT-GPR" on remaining filling material. Pro Taper had 12.96%, while Mani NRT-GPR had 24.26% (P=0.0056). memory: Research question: Effect of Radiofrequency Ablation (RFA) vs. Hepatic Resection on 5-year Disease-Free Survival (DFS). A randomized controlled trial [PMC3204557] found RFA had a 5-year DFS of 6.4% compared to 16.2% for resection (P = 0.037) in colorectal liver metastasis patients, using intraoperative ultrasound to assess tumor resectability. Other studies [PMC3872586, PMC5518918, PMC4562579] do not address this specific question. The results suggest hepatic resection may offer better DFS than RFA in this patient group.
text: A randomized controlled trial (PMC3204557) found that hepatic resection offers better 5-year disease-free survival (16.2%) compared to radiofrequency ablation (6.4%) in colorectal liver metastasis patients. This suggests hepatic resection may be more effective in improving long-term outcomes.

memory: This study assessed the therapeutic equivalence of SB4 (etanercept biosimilar) versus etanercept in RA patients on methotrexate. A three-way mixed model ANOVA evaluated PK endpoints (Ctrough, AUCτ), with a 95% CI of treatment difference (−9.41% to 4.98%) within the −15% to 15% equivalence margin, confirming equivalence. ADAs and NAbs were measured via immunoassays. Safety and immunogenicity were analyzed descriptively. Patients with RA, metabolic disorders, or medications affecting protein metabolism were excluded. Sample size was based on historical data. Ethics approval and informed consent were obtained.

outcome: therapeutic equivalence - Patients with moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis (RA) despite methotrexate (MTX) treatment

memory: The ADVANCE-D trial compared 15-pulse vs. 8-pulse ATP in managing ventricular tachycardia. Syncope/near-syncope occurred in 0.5% and 2.8% of FVT episodes in the 8-pulse group, and 3.2% and 0.7% in the 15-pulse group, with no significant difference (p = 0.690). memory: A randomized controlled trial compared a weight management intervention (diet, physical activity, plus usual care) with usual care on fiber intake at 12 months. The intervention included group sessions, booster meetings, and self-regulatory strategies, leading to a significant increase in fiber intake (M difference = 5.7 g/day, p < .001), with no change in fat consumption. These changes predicted weight loss. Allocation used opaque, sealed envelopes, and sessions were held in community venues. Participants received ESM-based feedback, and the intervention tested behavior change models with fidelity ensured.

memory: Participants received treatment as usual (TASU) with monthly booster sessions near GP surgeries, including psychopharmacological and psychotherapeutic interventions. Randomization used opaque envelopes and a random sequence generator. The intervention improved fiber intake, predicting weight loss at 4 and 12 months. Sessions focused on behavior adoption/maintenance with weekly tasks and feedback. Data from a pilot RCT in southwest England included qualitative data and fidelity checks. ESM procedures involved three days/week over six weeks, with fixed-format feedback. A pseudo-intervention group had equivalent contact time but no feedback. Exclusions included non-affective psychosis or recent manic episodes. Group activities focused on diet, physical activity, and self-monitoring, emphasizing intermediary effects. memory: The study compared maintaining 0.2 mg tamsulosin (nonescalators) versus escalating to 0.4 mg (escalators) on IIEF-5 scores in patients without LUTS improvement. No significant difference was observed (1.2 vs. 0.8, p=0.859). Additional assessments included PSA, urinalysis, TRUS, uroflowmetry, and PVR. Patients had physical exams, and adverse events were monitored. The study followed ethical guidelines and obtained informed consent. memory: In patients with no LUTS improvement, no significant difference in IIEF-5 scores was found between escalators (1.2) and nonescalators (0.8; p=0.859). memory: Gepotidacin, available orally and intravenously, is in phase II trials for ABSSSI and gonorrhea; nonclinical studies showed QT prolongation. It selectively inhibits bacterial DNA replication by targeting GyrA and ParC with minimal effect on human topoisomerase IIα. Adverse events included vomiting (15%), nausea (8%) at 1,800 mg. Tinnitus was self-reported, with unclear audiometric impact. Exclusion criteria included psychiatric disorders, substance use, and certain medications. Ethical guidelines were followed with informed consent. Cervical cytokine responses were analyzed via CBA and BCA post-Pap smear. Opioid-dependent patients had immune challenges due to confounding factors like infections and substance use. Protocols were approved by ethics boards.

Monkeys restrained with pole/collar device; rats from Taconic Farms. Pharmacokinetic assessments used ANCOVA. Surgical catheters allowed IV administration and repeated blood sampling. Survival studies euthanized moribund rats.

memory: A study evaluated the impact of "relevant computer tutorial = in sequence" versus "non-relevant tutorial = out of sequence" on knowledge of Oral Rehydration Solutions (ORS). In-sequence users scored 19% higher on ORS topics (95% CI +7%, +31%) with a large effect size (Cohen's-d = 0.85, 95% CI 0.25–1.5). Tutorials were accessed in a Pediatric Emergency Department (PED) on a single computer, with randomization after patient discussion. Time and interaction duration were recorded. Statistical methods included Cramer's V, Chi-square test, and confidence intervals. Participants were dental outpatients, and informed consent was obtained.

memory: JQJT tablets reduced the risk of pre-diabetes to diabetes conversion compared to placebo (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.384-0.876, P = 0.010), with lower incidence (16.5% vs 28.9%, P = 0.005) at 12 months. memory: A study compared bimatoprost 0.03% preservative-free (PF) with bimatoprost 0.03% (Lumigan) on intraocular pressure (IOP). memory: A study evaluated T-EO and Af-EO formulations against sterile water for overall effectiveness after 4 days. Both T-EO (26.27 ± 14.61%) and Af-EO (31.08 ± 16.52%) showed significantly lower biovolume than sterile water (51.35 ± 5.38%, P < 0.001). The trial was double-blind, randomized, and placebo-controlled, involving dental students from Universidad de Santiago de Compostela. T-EO lacks alcohol, while Af-EO includes alcohol and sodium fluoride. In situ antibacterial activity was assessed, emphasizing the need to preserve oral biofilm integrity. Results suggest both formulations have superior antibacterial effects compared to sterile water.

memory: UPBEAT was a UK multicenter RCT using MedSciNetTM to provide dietary guidance, recipes, and logbooks to pregnant women. Chronic constipation was treated with laxatives/enemas, while the comparator used oral sprays. Hypotension risk was assessed via logistic regression. Data were presented as mean ± SD or counts/percentages. Ethics approval was obtained.

memory: A study evaluated the effect of face-based attentional bias modification (ABM) versus placebo on anxious symptoms. ABM involved training participants to focus on positive cues by replacing negative stimuli with probes, while placebo ABM used balanced probe placement. Anxious symptoms, measured by the STAI trait subscale, significantly decreased in the ABM group (t(15) = 2.4, p = .03). The trial maintained blinding, and cortisol was measured via salivette. Reaction times assessed attentional bias. Ethics approval and informed consent were obtained. Results suggest face-based ABM may be more effective than placebo in reducing anxious symptoms.

memory: The study [PMC4497726] assessed the effect of 150 min/wk or 225 min/wk of aerobic exercise (AEx) versus no exercise on VO2 peak (% change). A dose-response increase in VO2 peak was observed in AEx groups. Participants were convenience sampled and evaluated for cognitive, cardiorespiratory, and functional health at baseline and post-intervention. The control group remained sedentary. Trainers monitored health and medication, and only prescribed exercise was allowed. The study aimed to evaluate AEx's dose-response effects on cognitive and functional outcomes in older adults.
text: Aerobic exercise (150 or 225 min/wk) significantly increased VO2 peak compared to no exercise (PMC4497726). A dose-response relationship was observed, with higher exercise volumes leading to greater improvements in cardiorespiratory fitness.

memory: The study [PMC4497726] shows a dose-response relationship between aerobic exercise (150 min/wk or 225 min/wk) and increased VO2 peak compared to no exercise, with higher volumes showing greater improvements. Adverse events were more common in the exercise groups. Cognitive improvements were consistent across groups, possibly due to practice effects. Other studies found no significant differences in quality-adjusted survival, clinical response rates, or biomarkers. These findings support the positive effect of aerobic exercise on VO2 peak with a dose-response pattern.

memory: The study compared progressive PSV discontinuation using SmartCare™ with respiratory physiotherapy–driven weaning. At extubation readiness, the physiotherapy group had higher PSV (8 vs. 5 cmH2O; p=0.015) and PEEP (8 vs. 5 cmH2O; p<0.001). Weaning duration was shorter in the physiotherapy group (60 [50–80] vs. 110 [80–130] minutes; p<0.001). No differences were found in Pimax, Pemax, FVC, or RSBI. Total ventilation duration and extubation failure rates were similar. Other studies found no significant differences in hydration, skin texture, weight, or lipid profile.

memory: A study compared intermediate progressive addition lenses (PALs) with distance single vision lenses on vertical toe clearance during stair ascent. Findings suggest intermediate PALs do not compromise stair ascent safety compared to distance single vision lenses.

memory: A study compared LPA (30 min moderate-intensity, 5-7 days/week) with FME (fibromyalgia education) on pain. LPA significantly reduced pain (P = .006; Cohen's d = .67) compared to FME. Participants were recruited from Johns Hopkins Arthritis Center and followed protocols including LPA training, self-monitoring, and symptom management. Daily activity and LPA types were recorded in diaries. Exclusions included those planning medication changes or seeking treatment for anxiety/depression. The control group received education without physical activity intervention. Participants were instructed not to alter physical activity outside the study. The trial was approved by Johns Hopkins IRB with informed consent obtained.

memory: A randomized, stratified trial compared nutrition psychoeducation (NPC) with usual care (UC) on triglyceride levels. NPC included education, motivational interviewing, and personalized feedback. LSD post-hoc analysis showed significantly lower triglycerides in NPC vs. UC (p=0.008). Informed consent was obtained, and ethical guidelines were followed. Data abstraction was performed by trained personnel using blinded records. Results suggest NPC may effectively reduce triglyceride levels compared to UC. Source: [PMC4236282].

memory: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial assessed JinqiJiangtang tablets (JQJT) for preventing progression from pre-diabetes to diabetes. Conducted in Chinese hospitals, participants received JQJT or placebo without knowledge of treatment. Results showed a 0.58-fold reduced risk of diabetes progression in the JQJT group [HR 0.58 (0.384, 0.876), P = 0.010]. Anti-diabetic drugs were excluded to avoid confounding. Other studies on CGM and diet were not directly relevant. These findings suggest JQJT may offer a potential intervention for pre-diabetes management.

memory: A study compared bimatoprost 0.03% preservative-free (PF) with bimatoprost 0.03% (Lumigan) on intraocular pressure (IOP). The formulations differed only in the absence of benzalkonium chloride in PF. IOP was measured as the mean of two or median of three readings. The between-group difference in mean worse eye IOP was <0.4 mm Hg at all time points, not statistically or clinically significant. Randomization was managed by Allergan Biostatistics, with identical medication kits for both formulations. Patients were excluded if pregnant, nursing, or could become pregnant. The study used ANOVA for analysis, with equivalence criteria similar to the primary analysis.

memory: A randomized controlled trial [PMC5518918] evaluated home-based training with telemonitoring versus centre-based training on peakVO2 in cardiac patients. Both groups showed significant improvements (home-based +15%, centre-based +11%, p < 0.01), with no significant between-group differences (p = 0.25). Home-based training included supervised sessions and weekly telefeedback, while centre-based training involved group sessions supervised by physical therapists. Patients were randomized using sealed envelopes, and heart rate monitors tracked training. No significant differences in adherence or outcomes were found. Ethical approval and informed consent were obtained. Additional studies [PMC3357231, PMC5726464, PMC3381083] confirmed adherence to ethical standards and data collection protocols.

A main effect was also significant (F(2,112) = 3.3, p = .05).
text: Face-based attentional bias modification significantly reduces anxious symptoms compared to placebo, as shown by a significant decrease in STAI trait scores (t(15) = 2.4, p = .03) (PMC3504298).

memory: A study showed that adding primaquine (PQ) to dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DHP) significantly reduced gametocyte carriage. At one week post-treatment, 2.1% of the DHP + PQ group had patent gametocytes, compared to 15% in the DHP-only group (prevalence ratio 0.12, 95% CI 0.02–0.9, p = 0.03). DHP alone had slow gametocyte clearance, with ongoing mosquito infection at two weeks. Membrane feeding assays showed reduced infectiousness to Anopheles dirus with PQ addition. Transmission in the region is low, heterogeneous, and seasonal. Source: [PMC5462369]

memory: A study compared SB4 (etanercept biosimilar) with etanercept (ETN) in RA patients on methotrexate for therapeutic equivalence. A three-way mixed model ANOVA showed a 95% CI for adjusted treatment difference (−9.41% to 4.98%), within the −15% to 15% equivalence margin, supporting equivalence. Patients with RA, diabetes, or metabolic disorders were excluded. Body composition was measured via body scans, and resistance exercise effects on muscle mass and strength were assessed. Written informed consent was obtained.

memory: The SCOPE trial, approved by the MHRA and conducted at the Wellcome Trust Clinical Research Facility, evaluated the feasibility of an RCT comparing colorectal cancer screening interventions in Ontario, Canada. Recruitment used telephone and mail follow-up, with eligibility assessed by study nurses. Biweekly venous blood samples were collected for metabolic, hematological, coagulation, and liver function analyses using flow cytometry. Genetic analysis of ~630,000 SNPs identified links with antihypertensive drug responses. Endometrial biopsies were collected via hysteroscopy and D&C, with participants randomized to LNG-IUS or NET, followed by clinic reviews and imaging. Pregnancy tests and eligibility checks were performed. Data were analyzed using statistical methods, including linear mixed-models.

memory: A study compared a weight management intervention (diet, physical activity, group sessions) with usual care, measuring fiber intake at 12 months. memory: A pilot RCT in southwest England evaluated a monthly booster intervention near GP surgeries, targeting behavior adoption, stress management, and self-monitoring. It improved fiber intake (M = 5.7 g/day, p < .001) and predicted weight loss at 4 and 12 months. Control groups received treatment as usual (antidepressants/mood stabilizers, with or without psychotherapy) or a pseudo-intervention (HDRS interviews). Exclusions included non-affective psychotic disorders or recent manic episodes. Group activities emphasized diet, physical activity, and skill-building.

Moderate events included vomiting (15%), nausea (8%), throat tightness (2%), and dizziness (2%), all occurring after 1,800 mg. Both doses caused a heart rate increase of 10–13 bpm. memory: Gepotidacin, tested in phase II for ABSSSI and gonorrhea, showed QT prolongation risks in nonclinical studies but selectively inhibits bacterial DNA replication via GyrA and ParC. At 1,800 mg, adverse events included vomiting, nausea, throat tightness, and dizziness. Tinnitus assessments relied on self-reports and faced sound masking challenges. Exclusion criteria included psychiatric/neurological disorders, substance use, and psychostimulant use. Ethical approvals and informed consent were obtained with blinding maintained. Cervical cytokine responses were measured using CBA and BCA assays, assessing Pap smear-induced inflammation. Opioid-dependent patients had confounding factors like infections and substance use. HPLC was used to measure free-form morphine and dextromethorphan levels.

memory: A study compared an area-wide computerized diabetes register with structured recall and individualized management to a standard system.
